title: No rel=canonical anywhere, and the vercel.app host serves the full site at 200
evidence:
NO rel=canonical IS EMITTED ON ANY ROUTE, AND BOTH HOSTS SERVE EVERY ARTICLE AT 200 AS INDEXABLE.

1. Root metadata has no canonical. app/layout.js:7-40:
   export const metadata = {
     metadataBase: new URL(siteMetadata.siteUrl),   // line 8
     title: {...}, description: ..., openGraph: {...}, twitter: {...},
     robots: { index: true, follow: true, googleBot: { index: true, follow: true, ... } },  // lines 30-39
   }
   No `alternates` key anywhere in the object.

2. The article route has no canonical. app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:20-53 generateMetadata returns only:
     title, description,
     openGraph: { ..., url: `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${slugStr}`, ... },   // line 40
     twitter: { ... }
   No `alternates`. Note line 40 concatenates onto a siteUrl that already ends in "/", so og:url ships a double slash (verified live below).

3. The only `alternates` in app/ is a feed, not a canonical. app/tags/[tag]/page.js:33-37:
     alternates: {
       types: {
         'application/rss+xml': `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/tags/${tag}/feed.xml`,
       },
     },

4. The one real canonical in the repo is unreachable dead code. components/SEO.js:140:
     <link rel="canonical" href={`${siteMetadata.siteUrl}${router.asPath}`} />
   It is inside `BlogSEO`, declared at components/SEO.js:70. `BlogSEO` is imported only at layouts/PostLayout.js:4 and layouts/PostSimple.js:4. No file imports PostLayout, PostSimple, or AuthorLayout. The sole PostLayout mention under app/ is the comment at app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:89 `// Build frontMatter object matching PostLayout expectations`. Note that components/SEO.js itself is NOT dead: pages/gallery.js:2 `import { PageSEO } from '@/components/SEO'`. `CommonSEO` (components/SEO.js:5-29) emits no canonical either, so the legacy gallery page also has none.

5. Wrong-host root cause. data/siteMetadata.js:9:
     siteUrl: 'https://sac-website.vercel.app/',
   This feeds metadataBase (app/layout.js:8), og:url, and the sitemap.

6. NO MITIGATION EXISTS. Verified absent: vercel.json (no such file); `redirects`/`rewrites`/`trailingSlash` in next.config.js (grep returns nothing); X-Robots-Tag in next.config.js securityHeaders; app/robots.js; app/sitemap.js; public/robots.txt. proxy.js is the Next 16 middleware and its `export const config = { matcher: [...] }` lists only /admin, /admin/:path*, /api/admin/:path*, /member, /member/:path*, /api/member/:path*, /auth/:path*, /api/auth/:path*. It never executes on /blog and contains zero host logic.

7. LIVE, read from the raw DOM in a real browser on 2026-08-23:
   | URL | HTTP | redirect | canonical | meta robots | X-Robots-Tag |
   | https://sac-website.vercel.app/blog/2026/08/19/captan-eclipse-solar-desde-marte | 200 | none | NONE | index, follow | null |
   | https://www.sociedadastronomia.com/blog/2026/08/19/captan-eclipse-solar-desde-marte | 200 | none | NONE | index, follow | null |
   | https://sac-website.vercel.app/ | 200 | none | NONE | - | - |
   | /robots.txt on BOTH hosts | 404 | - | - | - | null |
   Live og:url on BOTH hosts is the same string: `https://sac-website.vercel.app//blog/2026/08/19/captan-eclipse-solar-desde-marte` (double slash, vercel host).

8. NEW CORROBORATION I FOUND MYSELF, which raises the wrong-host risk: public/sitemap.xml declares 63 `<loc>` entries and every single one is on `https://sac-website.vercel.app//...` (63/63, with the double slash). It contains ZERO article URLs. Live fetch of /sitemap.xml on the production domain serves that same vercel-host file. So both published host signals, og:url and the sitemap, name the preview host rather than www.sociedadastronomia.com, while no canonical, no redirect, and no robots.txt exists to correct them.

CORRECT FIX ORDER: (a) set data/siteMetadata.js:9 to the production origin with NO trailing slash; (b) add a per-route self-referencing `alternates.canonical` in each generateMetadata (app/blog/[...slug]/page.js, app/tags/[tag]/page.js, app/blog/page/[page]/page.js, app/media/[slug]/page.js) rather than a single inherited root canonical, since Next.js propagates a parent layout's `alternates.canonical` to children that do not override it; (c) 308 any `*.vercel.app` Host to the production origin, via a redirect rule or by widening the proxy.js matcher; (d) delete only layouts/PostLayout.js, layouts/PostSimple.js and layouts/AuthorLayout.js, and keep components/SEO.js until pages/gallery.js:2 stops importing PageSEO from it.
impact: Every article exists at two indexable origins (www.sociedadastronomia.com and sac-website.vercel.app) with byte-identical HTML and zero canonical signal. Google must guess which host owns each of the 77 articles; link equity splits, and the wrong host can win the SERP. This is the single largest indexation risk in the metadata layer.
fix: Add a self-referencing canonical to the root and to every dynamic route. In app/layout.js add `alternates: { canonical: '/' }` (Next resolves it against metadataBase). In app/blog/[...slug]/page.js generateMetadata add `alternates: { canonical: `/blog/${slugStr}` }`. Same for app/tags/[tag]/page.js (`/tags/${tag}`), app/blog/page/[page]/page.js (`/blog/page/${page}`), and app/media/[slug]/page.js. Separately, block the preview host: add a Vercel redirect or a middleware that 308s any request whose Host is `*.vercel.app` to the same path on www.sociedadastronomia.com. Delete the dead layouts/PostLayout.js, PostSimple.js, AuthorLayout.js and components/SEO.js so the two competing SEO systems stop coexisting.

title: Trailing slash on siteUrl produces a double slash in og:url, JSON-LD url and RSS links
evidence:
Root cause, verified: data/siteMetadata.js:9 `siteUrl: 'https://sac-website.vercel.app/',` (trailing slash).

Article-facing callers, verified verbatim:
- app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:41 `url: `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${slugStr}`,` (openGraph.url)
- app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:110 `url: `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${slugStr}`,` (JSON-LD Article url)

Other callers, verified verbatim:
- app/feed.xml/route.js:9 `<guid>${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${post.slug}</guid>`
- app/feed.xml/route.js:11 `<link>${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${post.slug}</link>`
- app/feed.xml/route.js:34 `<link>${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog</link>`
- app/feed.xml/route.js:40 `<atom:link href="${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/feed.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/>`
- app/tags/[tag]/page.js:35 `'application/rss+xml': `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/tags/${tag}/feed.xml`,`
- scripts/generate-sitemap.js:36 `<loc>${siteMetadata.siteUrl}${route}</loc>` -> public/sitemap.xml line 4 `<loc>https://sac-website.vercel.app//gallery</loc>`; `grep -c "app//" public/sitemap.xml` = 63, i.e. every loc in the committed sitemap.

Why Next does not fix it (node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/resolvers/resolve-url.js, read directly):
- :73-77 `try { const parsedUrl = new URL(url); return parsedUrl; } catch {}` — an absolute string skips metadataBase joining entirely.
- :109 `resolvedUrl = result.pathname === '/' && result.searchParams.size === 0 ? result.origin : result.href` — pathname is `//blog/x`, so href is returned unchanged.
- Reproduced: `new URL('https://sac-website.vercel.app//blog/x').href` === `https://sac-website.vercel.app//blog/x`, pathname `//blog/x`.

Correction to the original evidence: og:image on App Router pages is NOT affected. socialBanner is relative, so it takes resolve-url.js:83 `path.posix.join(metadataBase.pathname, url)`, which collapses `/` + `/static/...` to `/static/...`; verified in node the result is `https://sac-website.vercel.app/static/images/x.png` (single slash). The double-slash og:image on /gallery is real but originates in components/SEO.js:32-33 `const ogImageUrl = siteMetadata.siteUrl + siteMetadata.socialBanner` (Pages Router, reached only via pages/gallery.js), not the App Router metadata path.

Mitigation search (all negative): no normalizeUrl / absUrl / slash-collapse regex / trailingSlash anywhere outside node_modules; no vercel.json; no rewrite in next.config.js; app/layout.js:8 `metadataBase: new URL(siteMetadata.siteUrl)` is bypassed for absolute strings.

Live behaviour, measured: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' https://sac-website.vercel.app//gallery` returns `308 https://sac-website.vercel.app/gallery`. The double-slash form is never served, so it cannot be indexed as a duplicate. Residual harm: all 63 sitemap locs are redirects (Search Console reports them as "Page with redirect"), social scrapers take an extra hop from og:url, and RSS guid/link plus JSON-LD url carry a third URL variant.

Fix: delete the trailing slash at data/siteMetadata.js:9, regenerate public/sitemap.xml, and optionally add `export const absUrl = (p) => new URL(p, siteMetadata.siteUrl).toString()` used at app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:41 and :110, app/feed.xml/route.js:9,11,34,40, app/tags/[tag]/page.js:35, and components/SEO.js:32-33 so a future trailing slash cannot reintroduce it.
impact: The declared og:url and schema.org url for every article are a third URL form that neither host serves directly (it 308-redirects). Rich-result validators compare schema url against the crawled URL and see a mismatch; social scrapers follow an extra redirect hop; and any consumer that trusts the string builds a third duplicate URL variant.
fix: Drop the trailing slash in data/siteMetadata.js:9. Optionally harden the callers with a helper, e.g. `export const absUrl = (p) => new URL(p, siteMetadata.siteUrl).toString()`, and use it at app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:41 and :110 and in app/feed.xml/route.js so a future trailing slash cannot reintroduce this.

    description: siteMetadata.description,
    url: siteMetadata.siteUrl,
    siteName: siteMetadata.title,      // :18  lost on article pages
    images: [siteMetadata.socialBanner],

  },
app/layout.js:23-29 root twitter:

    site: '@soc_astrocaribe',          // :25  lost on article pages

app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:35-49 replaces both objects wholesale:
      openGraph: {
        title: article.title,
        description: article.summary,
        type: 'article',
        publishedTime: article.date,
        modifiedTime: article.lastmod || article.date,
        url: `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/blog/${slugStr}`,
        images: article.images || [siteMetadata.socialBanner],

Net loss on every article page: og:site_name, og:locale, twitter:site. Nothing else is dropped (title, description, url, type, images, twitter:card are all re-supplied).

Mitigation ruled out:
- No layout between root and the article page: only app/layout.js, app/admin/layout.js, app/member/layout.js exist (verified via find over app/).
- components/SEO.js:14 `<meta property="og:site_name" .../>` and :23 `<meta name="twitter:site" .../>` are unreachable from this route. - app/layout.js:45 `<html lang="es" suppressHydrationWarning>` already supplies the language signal search engines actually use, so the og:locale loss has no search impact.
- data/siteMetadata.js:23 `twitter: 'https://twitter.com/soc_astrocaribe'` is a URL, not a handle, so SEO.js:23 would have emitted a malformed twitter:site anyway.

app/about/page.js:11-14

    description: 'Conoce al equipo de la Sociedad de Astronomia del Caribe',

app/brand/page.js:10-13 (same shape, template strings using siteMetadata.headerTitle)

The root supplies the fields that are lost, app/layout.js:14-22:

    description: siteMetadata.description,
    url: siteMetadata.siteUrl,
    siteName: siteMetadata.title,
    images: [siteMetadata.socialBanner],
    locale: 'es_PR',

Mechanism confirmed in the installed Next.js 16.2.3, not inferred.
node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/resolve-metadata.js:169-185, inside `for (const key_ in metadata)`:
  case 'openGraph': {
    newResolvedMetadata.openGraph = convertUrlsToStrings(await resolveOpenGraph(metadata.openGraph, metadataBase, pathname, metadataContext, titleTemplates.openGraph))
    break

The assignment overwrites, it never merges with the parent. Because the loop iterates only keys present in the page object, omitting openGraph keeps the parent object untouched.

node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/resolvers/resolve-opengraph.js, resolveOpenGraph:
  const resolved = { ...openGraph, title: resolveTitle(openGraph.title, titleTemplate) }
  resolveProps(resolved, openGraph)            // sets target.images = resolveImages(og.images, ...) -> undefined
  resolved.url = openGraph.url ? resolveAbsoluteUrlWithPathname(...) : null
Nothing reads the parent, so images, url, siteName, locale and type are absent on these six routes.

Twitter divergence confirmed at node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/resolve-metadata.js:619-636, postProcessMetadata:
  const hasTwTitle = hasTitle(twitter)
  if (!hasTwTitle) { ... }
The root sets twitter.title at app/layout.js:26, so hasTwTitle is true and no autofill runs. The inherited twitter:title stays 'Sociedad de Astronomía del Caribe' while og:title is the page name.

No mitigation exists. `find app pages public -iname "opengraph-image*" -o -iname "twitter-image*"` returns nothing, and `grep -rn "openGraph" app/ lib/ components/ data/ pages/` returns only app/layout.js, the six files above, and app/blog/[...slug]/page.js.

Scope limit. Blog articles are not affected: app/blog/[...slug]/page.js:35-43 sets openGraph with type: 'article', url and images, plus its own twitter block at 44-49.

Correct fix, the delete-the-block option in the original proposal is wrong. Removing openGraph leaves the parent's resolved object intact, which would set og:title to the site name on all six pages. Export a shared base from data/siteMetadata.js or a small helper and spread it: openGraph: { ...baseOpenGraph, title, description, url: `${siteUrl}about` }, with a matching twitter: { ...baseTwitter, title, description }.
impact: Sharing /about, /events, /guides, /brand, /contact or /weather produces a bare text card with no image on Facebook, WhatsApp and LinkedIn — the channels this organisation actually uses. The og:title vs twitter:title mismatch means X shows the site name while Facebook shows the page name for the same link.

Add a matching `twitter: { ...baseTwitter, title, description }` so the two never diverge.

title: Every tag page advertises an RSS feed that returns 404, backed by 62 stale gitignored files
evidence:
CONFIRMED CORE DEFECT:
app/tags/[tag]/page.js:33-37 (verified verbatim):
    alternates: {
      types: {
        'application/rss+xml': `${siteMetadata.siteUrl}/tags/${tag}/feed.xml`,
      },
    },
No route serves that path. `find app -type f` under app/tags returns exactly two files: app/tags/page.js and app/tags/[tag]/page.js. `find app -iname "*feed*"` returns only app/feed.xml (the site-wide feed at app/feed.xml/route.js:40). There is no middleware file at the repo root and no rewrites/redirects in next.config.js (grep for "rewrite|redirect|trailingSlash" returns nothing), so nothing intercepts the URL. Result: every tag page ships a head link to a 404.
The href is also malformed: data/siteMetadata.js:9 is `siteUrl: 'https://sac-website.vercel.app/'` (trailing slash), so the emitted href is `https://sac-website.vercel.app//tags/<tag>/feed.xml` with a double slash.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL EVIDENCE:
1. Wrong line cited. The ignore rule is .gitignore:19 `*.xml` with .gitignore:20 `!app/**`, not .gitignore:26. Verified by `git check-ignore -v public/tags/asteroide/feed.xml` -> `.gitignore:19:*.xml`.
2. Wrong dates. Not all 62 files date to 2026-02-12; public/tags/lunar/feed.xml is 2025-01-26.
3. The stale-file half of the finding has no SEO weight. `git ls-files public/tags` returns 0 AND `git log --oneline -- public/tags` returns nothing, so those 62 files were never committed and never deployed. Files absent from the deploy cannot be crawled, so their malformed content at public/tags/asteroide/feed.xml:5 and :11 is a local-only artifact, not a search problem.
4. The sitemap-causation claim is false. Because public/tags/**/*.xml was never tracked, the `'public/tags/**/*.xml'` glob at scripts/generate-sitemap.js:12 never contributed URLs to any deployed sitemap. The local public/sitemap.xml (63 <loc> entries, itself gitignored at .gitignore:14) is a local-only file. In a clean checkout the glob resolves to pages/404.js + pages/gallery.js only, and 404 is dropped at scripts/generate-sitemap.js:31, so the deployed sitemap has one URL. That collapse is caused by the empty data/blog/ corpus, not by the tag feeds. Attributing "the site's total sitemap failure" to this finding is a misattribution and belongs to the separate sitemap finding.
5. Do not assert a page count. generateStaticParams at app/tags/[tag]/page.js:10-25 derives tags from S3 via listArticles, so neither "61" nor "62" tag pages can be verified from the repo. The correct statement is "every generated tag page".
impact: Every one of the 61 tag pages ships a broken `<link rel="alternate">` in its head, which feed readers and crawlers follow to a 404. Because scripts/generate-sitemap.js:12 globs those absent files, the deployed sitemap collapses from 63 URLs to a single one (`pages/gallery.js` -> /gallery), which is the mechanism behind the site's total sitemap failure.
fix: Either delete the `alternates` block at app/tags/[tag]/page.js:33-37 and drop `'public/tags/**/*.xml'` from scripts/generate-sitemap.js:12, or implement a real app/tags/[tag]/feed.xml/route.js modelled on app/feed.xml/route.js that filters `listArticles` by the kebab-cased tag. Delete the 62 stale local directories under public/tags/ either way. Replace scripts/generate-sitemap.js entirely with an app/sitemap.js that reads from S3.
